cohort: The study involved 200 women with a history of one previous cesarean section who were delivering at a tertiary care center, grouped by their current delivery method.
finding: Women who underwent vaginal delivery had significantly shorter hospital stays and lower neonatal ICU admission rates compared to those who had a cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery in women with a previous cesarean section is associated with shorter hospital stays and potentially better neonatal outcomes in terms of Apgar scores and reduced ICU admissions.
